verdict: The longest chain we ran: words became a sheet that passed the picture check, a textured mesh, a rig with two motions, a built street, and a shot where H3 follows the exact depth of the Blender render. The man keeps his jacket and build all the way. Two flaws: the shop signs carry gibberish lettering, and from behind the mesh's head is a smooth blank shape, because the sheet only shows the front. We checked the score by measurement only.
peak_note: Peak is this run's own ComfyUI and tools, read from nvidia-smi every 2 seconds. The card was shared with other work. Time adds up each stage's own work, not the wait for the shared card.

values.who: a courier in his forties, broad shoulders, close-cropped grey hair, a rust-orange canvas work jacket, dark green trousers, heavy brown boots

stages.label: Character sheet
stages.does: Draws the invented adult once, front on, and runs the picture check over it.

stages.label: Mesh, rig, motion
stages.does: TRELLIS.2 builds the mesh from the sheet, SkinTokens rigs it, Kimodo writes each motion from words, and Blender assembles one file.
stages.note: From behind, the head is a smooth blank shape: the sheet only shows the front.

stages.label: The set
stages.does: A real-scale street, built in Blender from a brief.
stages.licence: GPL, runs as a separate tool
stages.prompt: a quiet downtown street at golden hour with old brick shopfronts

stages.label: The shot
stages.does: Blender renders the blocked shot, and H3 follows its exact depth.
stages.note: The shop signs on the left carry gibberish lettering. Its time includes Blender's CPU passes and any wait for the shared card inside the shot; we didn't split those out.
stages.prompt: A courier in a rust-orange work jacket walks down a quiet brick street toward the camera at golden hour. The shop signs are plain painted boards with no lettering.
